prompt: Write 10 distinct short extracts of Larkmere Mutual's official guidance, procedures or policy wording about: a claim made by the executor of an estate. Two to four sentences each, in the society's own formal voice. Use type "fact". Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"Where the policyholder has died, a claim may be made by the executor or personal representative of the estate, provided we are satisfied they are acting lawfully. We may ask for a sealed copy of the grant of probate or letters of administration before we discuss the claim in detail. Until we have seen evidence of authority, we will only communicate with the appointed representative about the claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"An executor must provide evidence that they are entitled to act for the estate before we can settle a claim or issue payment. If more than one executor has been appointed, we may require confirmation that all executors agree to the claim instructions. We will not make payment to an individual executor unless the policy terms or the estate documents allow us to do so."},{"type":"fact","content":"Claims made by an executor will be handled under the policy that was in force at the time of the insured event, subject to the estate proving its authority. The death of the policyholder does not remove the need to meet the normal policy conditions, including notice of claim, evidence of loss and co-operation with our enquiries. We may ask for additional documents where ownership of the insured property or item is not clear."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where the claim concerns a home occupied by the deceased, the executor must tell us if the property is unoccupied, being sold or being let. This may affect the cover available, the security requirements and the steps we expect to be taken to protect the property. Failure to keep the property secure may prejudice the claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"For motor claims, an executor may submit the claim on behalf of the estate if the deceased was the registered keeper or owner of the vehicle. We may require the vehicle keys, V5C registration document and proof of estate authority before authorising repairs or disposal. If the vehicle is written off, any settlement will be paid to the estate unless we agree otherwise in writing."},{"type":"fact","content":"If a claim payment is due to the estate, we will normally pay the executor or personal representative named in the probate documents. Where the estate is subject to a solicitor’s client account, we may make payment to that account on request and on receipt of suitable authority. We will not usually divide the payment between beneficiaries."},{"type":"fact","content":"An executor must tell us whether the deceased had any joint policyholders, joint owners or other parties with an interest in the insured property. We may need to confirm how that interest affects the claim and who is entitled to receive any settlement. If the estate cannot establish title to the item or property claimed for, the claim may be declined."},{"type":"fact","content":"We may require a certified copy of the will, the death certificate and identification for the executor before proceeding with a claim made on behalf of an estate. Where probate is not yet available, we may place the claim on hold until the necessary authority is produced. This is to prevent payment to a person who does not have the legal right to act."},{"type":"fact","content":"The executor must keep accurate records of all correspondence, valuations, invoices and repair estimates relating to the claim. We may ask for these documents at any stage and may inspect damaged property before settlement. If the estate disposes of relevant property before we have had the opportunity to assess it, this may affect the amount we pay."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where a claim is made after the death of the policyholder, our liability is limited to the extent of the policy cover and the estate’s lawful interest. Any excess, unpaid premium or recovery action will be dealt with in the usual way and may be set against the settlement. The executor remains responsible for responding promptly to requests for information and for telling us about any change in circumstances."}]}
